skill.name: obsidian-bases
skill.description: Create and edit Obsidian Bases .base files with valid YAML views, filters, formulas, property displays, and summaries for note collections.
skill.summary: Build database-like Obsidian views from notes with filters, formulas, and summaries.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: Review found the static findings to be false positives caused by Markdown backticks, YAML code fences, formula examples, and official Obsidian documentation links. No evidence found of executable scripts, command execution instructions, data exfiltration, prompt injection, or unsafe network behavior in SKILL.md.

content.user_title: Build Obsidian Bases for Dynamic Notes
content.value_statement: Obsidian Bases can be hard to write correctly by hand. This skill helps create valid views, filters, formulas, and summaries.
actual_capabilities: Creates .base structures with global filters, views, formulas, property displays, and summaries.
Builds table, cards, list, and map view configurations for Obsidian note collections.
Uses Obsidian file metadata, note properties, formula properties, and documented formula functions.
Provides patterns for task trackers, reading lists, project notes, and daily note indexes.
Explains YAML quoting rules and Markdown embedding syntax for Bases.
limitations: Does not run Obsidian or validate files inside a live vault.
Cannot confirm that optional community plugins are installed.
Requires accurate property names and workflow goals from the user.
Focuses on Obsidian Bases, not general Obsidian plugin development.

use_cases.title: Organize Project Notes
use_cases.description: Create a Base that groups project notes by status, owner, due date, and recent activity.

use_cases.title: Track Reading Lists
use_cases.description: Build card and table views for books, articles, authors, pages, covers, and reading status.

use_cases.title: Index Daily Notes
use_cases.description: Generate a filtered view of daily notes with dates, word estimates, and modified times.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Base
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first .base file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian Base for my project notes. Include a table view, a status filter, and columns for file name, owner, due date, and status.

prompt_templates.title: Add Reading Views
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Obsidian Base for my reading list. Include a cards view for covers and a table view for author, pages, status, and estimated reading time.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Formulas and Summaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Update my existing Base plan with formulas for overdue tasks, priority labels, days until due, and summary rows for task counts and average days remaining.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Base
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Obsidian Base design for invalid filters, confusing property names, missing summaries, and YAML quoting issues. Suggest a cleaner version.

output_examples.input: Create a task tracker base for notes tagged task.
output_examples.output: A ready-to-save Base configuration with active and completed task views, due-date formulas, priority labels, and summary settings.

output_examples.input: Make a reading dashboard for books and articles.
output_examples.output: A Base design with card and table views, author and page fields, status filters, and estimated reading-time formulas.

output_examples.input: Review my daily notes Base idea.
output_examples.output: A cleaner daily-note index plan with date-based filtering, filename matching, word estimates, and practical column ordering.

best_practices: Provide real property names from your vault before asking for filters or formulas.
Start with one table view, then add cards, lists, summaries, or grouping as needed.
Ask for YAML quoting checks when formulas contain nested strings or comparison operators.
anti_patterns: Do not request a Base without explaining which notes should be included.
Do not mix unrelated workflows into one Base when separate views would be clearer.
Do not assume formula property names exist before defining them in the Base.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates and edits Obsidian Bases .base files with views, filters, formulas, properties, and summaries.

faq.question: Can it validate a Base inside Obsidian?
faq.answer: No. It can help produce valid YAML, but Obsidian must still load and validate the file.

faq.question: Which view types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers table, cards, list, and map views as documented in the skill.

faq.question: Can it use my existing note properties?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide property names such as status, due, author, cover, or priority for better output.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-based and only includes links to Obsidian reference pages.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
